title: The Escarpment of the Upper Fly River
premise: Mara Ishikawa, captain of the riverboat Kestrel, takes a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise to deliver his findings to a daughter he abandoned. The map points to a wrecked colonial steamer sunk in the Upper Fly River gorge, laden with gold and evidence of a massacre the salvage fleet's owner helped commit. Racing six tides before the concession permits expire, Mara assembles a crew of outcasts who become the family none of them had, while the fleet's enforcer burns villages and buys witnesses to bury the past. In the climax, Mara reaches the wreck on the final tide, recovers the massacre ledger, and forces a reckoning by giving it to the victims' descendants rather than the courts, choosing justice outside the law. She delivers the prospector's letter to his daughter, keeps nothing for herself but the boat and her crew, and learns that survival is only worth its price when it is shared.
about_author: Freya Kavanagh spent a decade working supply runs on Papua New Guinea's river systems before turning to fiction full-time. Her novels draw on oral histories gathered in river towns, and she now writes from a stilt house in Queensland with her partner and an ill-tempered kelpie.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A routine cargo run down the Fly establishes Mara's intimate knowledge of the river and her isolation after her brother's death left her the Kestrel and its debts. When she finds prospector Elias Vane gut-shot on a mudbank, the emotional beat is wary compassion: she takes him aboard against her own rule about strangers.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, fading in and out. Dying below decks, he trades Mara a wax-cloth map of the Upper Fly gorge and a brass key for one promise: bring what he found to his daughter Nell in Port Moresby. He hints at a wreck, gold, and 'the thing that should have hung me.' Beat: guilt transmuted into trust.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Burying Elias at a bend he loved, Mara studies the map and realizes the wreck predates any permit — meaning whatever's inside belongs to no concession. Her engineer, old Tamu, recognizes the steamer's name: Meridian, lost in '09 with witnesses aboard. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the Kiunga registry she learns the Corrigan Salvage Fleet holds permits expiring in six tides; if the wreck isn't claimed and logged by then, the gorge reverts to customary owners. She also spots Corrigan's enforcer, Deacon Rill, buying drinks and asking after a dead prospector. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Mara recruits a found-family crew: Nell Vane herself, who arrives angry and armed with questions; diver Sefina, blacklisted from the fleet for refusing to falsify a survey; and runaway deckhand Pita. Each has been priced out or burned by Corrigan. Beat: reluctant kinship forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Rill Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: Deacon Rill's POV. Rill inspects the Kestrel under pretext of a safety check, probing for the map. Mara lies well, but Rill leaves a listening device in the engine room, which Tamu finds. Beat: cold dread — the enemy is patient, polite, and thorough.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Clock
chapters.summary: Sefina's POV. The Kestrel fights the gorge's first rapids; Sefina teaches Mara's crew her diving craft while Nell interrogates Mara about her father. Nell's fury softens when Mara produces Elias's unopened letters. Beat: trust tested by current and confession alike.

chapters.title: The Burned Village
chapters.summary: Pita's POV. They find a riverside village razed, survivors scattered — Rill clearing witnesses along the route. Among the ashes, an elder gives Pita a carved token, saying the river remembers who owes whom. Beat: the stakes turn from treasure to blood debt.

chapters.title: Dead Reckoning
chapters.summary: Tamu's POV. Sabotage discovered — someone has loosened the fuel lines during a portage. Tamu repairs it while rationing what remains, calculating they can make the wreck but not the return. Beat: quiet sacrifice; Tamu tells no one how thin the margin is.

chapters.title: Nell's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Reading her father's letters, Nell learns Elias witnessed the Meridian massacre as a young deckhand and was paid to stay silent — the gold was hush money he could never spend. Beat: forgiveness arriving too late to give him, redirected toward finishing his errand.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Shadow
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Corrigan's lead salvage barge appears downstream, running lights dark. Mara plays a desperate trick, anchoring decoy lanterns in a side channel and slipping past in fog. Beat: triumph laced with fear — Rill knows exactly where they're headed now.

chapters.title: Sefina's Descent
chapters.summary: Sefina's POV. First dive on the Meridian in the gorge's green gloom: the hull intact, gold cases visible, and human remains arranged with terrible deliberateness near the strongroom. Sefina surfaces shaking, having seen scratch marks inside — some survived the sinking briefly. Beat: horror reframing the prize.

chapters.title: The Strongroom Key
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Elias's brass key opens the strongroom, but inside there's no fortune — instead, a ship's ledger naming every man paid for the massacre, signed by Corrigan's father, plus the gold meant to buy silence. Beat: the treasure was always the truth; the gold is the leash attached.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Crew debate: sell the ledger to a newspaper, ransom it to Corrigan, or honor customary law and give it to the descendants' council upstream. Nell argues for the council — her father's debt must be paid where it was incurred. Beat: the theme crystallizes into choice.

chapters.title: Rill's Offer
chapters.summary: Rill's POV. Rill corners the Kestrel at a narrows and offers Mara triple the gold's value and clean papers for everyone — the same deal, he admits, that bought Elias. Mara refuses, and Rill, almost respectfully, promises to take it from her corpse. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Pita's POV. Rill's men attack at dawn; the Kestrel's crew fights a running battle through the rapids. Tamu is gravely wounded holding the engine room, and Pita — the boy nobody trusted with anything — saves the boat with a helm maneuver Sefina taught him. Beat: found family proven in fire.

chapters.title: The Last Tide Begins
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With hours left on the permits, Corrigan himself arrives by floatplane, planning to log the wreck legally and destroy the ledger in the same visit. Mara realizes the only way to beat both clock and company is to move the evidence tonight, on the falling tide. Beat: cornered clarity.

chapters.title: Descent into the Hold
chapters.summary: Sefina and Nell's alternating POV. Night dive to recover the ledger and the massacre victims' effects for their families, while Rill's divers close in. Sefina stays behind to jam the strongroom hatch, trapping Rill's lead diver, and barely escapes the collapse. Beat: courage at the edge of drowning.

chapters.title: Corrigan's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Climax. Mara confronts Corrigan on his own barge, ledger open, crew and the descendants' council witnesses standing behind her. She doesn't blackmail him — she reads the names aloud until his own crew step away from him, and lets the river towns decide what happens next. Beat: justice outside the law, delivered without a shot.

chapters.title: What the Current Takes
chapters.summary: Tamu's POV, convalescent. Corrigan flees upriver and is arrested at the coast by officials who can no longer ignore notarized copies already sent ahead; Rill vanishes into the interior, owed a debt the river may collect. The permits lapse; the gorge passes to the customary owners. Beat: cost tallied, order restored but not tidy.

chapters.title: Nell's Answer
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. In Port Moresby, Nell delivers her father's last letter to herself, reading it aloud at his grave marker she finally commissions. She accepts a place on the Kestrel's crew rather than the inheritance she could claim. Beat: grief resolved into belonging.

chapters.title: Every Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The Kestrel runs cargo again, crewed by strays who became family, the ledger's copies circulating where they'll do harm to the guilty. Mara passes the bend where Elias is buried and finally answers his promise aloud: done. Beat: peace earned, the river forgiving nothing but carrying them forward anyway.
